messages:
derek: Heads up — after pushing kernel 5.10.102 + CUDA 11.8 to us-west-2-gpu nodes we're seeing pods stuck in Init:DriverSetup. Device plugin logs show registration timeouts.

sophia: seeing the same on a couple of node pools here. Scheduler keeps retrying and pods never become Runnable.

raj: can you paste device-plugin logs? wondering if it's the plugin image we rolled or the driver install step.

maria: short dump from a failing node (trimmed):
```
May 21 08:12:01 gpu-node-12 kubelet[2456]: E0521 08:12:01.123456 2456 device_plugin.go:258] registration failed: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded
May 21 08:12:01 gpu-node-12 nvidia-device-plugin: time="2026-05-21T08:12:01Z" level=error msg="driver probe returned incompatible version: driver=525.105.17 cuda=12.0 expected>=11.8"
```

derek: we upgraded drivers to 525.105.17 via dkms, and CUDA runtime 11.8 from the installer. The device-plugin image is `nv-device-plugin:v0.12.0` which we just promoted.

raj: nv-device-plugin v0.12.0 added stricter driver/CUDA compatibility checks and a probe reorder (see changelog). That could trigger registration failures if the kernel module isn't fully loaded before the plugin starts.

sophia: timeline: kernel rollout (5.10.102) finished ~07:50, drivers installed via node-init at 07:55, plugin rollout at 08:00. Might be a race where plugin starts before nvidia persistence daemon finishes.

maria: quick reproducer: restart kubelet on node after driver install -> device-plugin fails to register for ~30s, then succeeds. But for some nodes it never recovers and scheduler marks GPUs as 0 allocatable.

ops-jenkins: infra-bot: triggered rollback job for nv-device-plugin to v0.11.3 in us-west-2 (job #3482).

infra-bot: rollback initiated: nv-device-plugin -> v0.11.3 on 6 daemonset pods. Watch: https://ci.redwood/infra/3482

raj: rolling back plugin is a reasonable short-term mitigation. Longer-term we need either: a) make driver install + module load deterministic before plugin start, or b) change plugin to be more tolerant of transient probe failures.

derek: also seeing increased NCCL errors in distributed workloads around the same time: network peer discovery failing with "NCCL WARN NET/Socket : maps mismatch". Might be correlated — when a node loses GPU allocatable mid-job NCCL rings break.

sophia: that explains the spike in failed training runs & cost from auto-retries. Cost team pinged me about a 3x increase in GPU hours this morning.

maria: short-term checklist I ran:
1) cordon affected nodes
2) restart kubelet + ensure nvidia modules loaded (`lsmod | grep nvidia`)
3) restart device-plugin pod
4) uncordon when allocatable shows GPUs

I automated steps 2+3 as a script and ran it on 8 nodes, 6 recovered.

raj: can we add a kubelet systemd dependency so device-plugin waits for nvidia-modprobe.service? On node images we could add `After=nvidia-modprobe.service` to the kubelet unit and ensure driver-install hooks enable that.

derek: good idea. Another option: change device-plugin daemonset to use `restartPolicy: Always` + startupProbe with longer initialDelay to let drivers finish. But that doesn't help nodes where module fails to load due to kernel headers mismatch.

sophia: we found 2 nodes where DKMS build failed (kernel-headers mismatch) — logs show module build error. Those nodes need reimage or pinned kernel headers.

maria: action items:
- raj: roll forward a kubelet systemd patch to staging node image and test (ETA 2d)
- ops: finish plugin rollback to v0.11.3 in us-west-2 and monitor (in progress)
- derek/sophia: add alert for device-plugin registration failures (alert already exists but threshold too high)
- maria: share recovery script to runbook

raj: also let's add a node-level annotation when kernel + driver mismatch is detected so autoscaling avoids scheduling GPU jobs there. e.g., `gpu.redwood/incompatible-driver=true`. Admission webhook could deny pod creation on annotated nodes for now.

derek: agreed. We should also add a per-cluster preflight that checks kernel headers + DKMS build for new node images before pushing to prod.

sophia: for the NCCL issue I'm going to add a guard in our training infra to fail fast if < expected GPU count present on startup, to avoid long-running allreduce failures.

maria: rollout status: rollback to v0.11.3 completed on 6/6 ds pods at 08:40; device-plugin registration errors dropped by 90% within 10m. NCCL errors also trended down after node recoveries.

ops-jenkins: noted rollback job finished: https://ci.redwood/infra/3482 ✅

raj: follow-ups for next week: add kubelet dependency, node annotation + webhook, improve device-plugin startupProbe, and preflight tests in image pipeline.

derek: thanks team — adding tasks to eng-infra board. If you see any lingering nodes with zero GPUs, ping me directly. :thumbsup:
